answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power in proportion to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than counting accounts. Whether an agent trades onyx, maps a lagoon, or manages an orchard, creating extra identities adds no voting power: splitting 100 locked tokens among 100 accounts still yields only 100 votes. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
